auth.description: Sentry auth token sent as a bearer — an organization, user or internal-integration token
auth.name: sentry.auth_token
auth.subject: unstated

description: Sentry error tracking: read an issue and its latest event, triage an issue, read a project

operations.description: Get one issue — its title, culprit, level, status, assignee, first and last seen timestamps and event counts. An issue is Sentry's group of like events, not a single occurrence; use `sentry-issue-event-latest` for the stack trace

params.description: The organization's slug as it appears in a Sentry URL (`acme-inc`), or its numeric id
params.name: organization_id_or_slug

params.description: The issue's numeric id — the number in a Sentry issue URL, and the `issue_id` an alert payload carries. It is not the short id (`ACME-INC-7F`)
params.name: issue_id

assignedTo.description: Who owns it: `{type: "user"|"team", id, name, email}`, or null when unassigned

count.description: How many events are grouped in this issue — **a STRING, not a number**, per Sentry's own schema (its example is `"150"`). Compare it as a number only after converting

culprit.description: Where Sentry attributes it — a function or transaction name. Null when it cannot attribute one

firstSeen.description: When the first event of this group arrived

id.description: The issue's numeric id, as a string

isUnhandled.description: True when the error was not caught by application code

lastSeen.description: When the most recent one did. This, not `count`, is what says whether the issue is still live

level.description: The severity of the grouped events

metadata.description: Sentry's own grouping metadata — typically `{type, value, filename, function}`. Free-form in the vendor's schema, so no member is declared

permalink.description: The issue's page in Sentry — the link to give a human

priority.description: `low`, `medium`, `high` or null — Sentry's own computed priority, distinct from `level`

project.description: Which project it belongs to: `{id, name, slug, platform}`. Its `slug` is what `sentry-project-get` takes

shortId.description: The human-facing id shown in Sentry's UI and in alert emails, e.g. `ACME-INC-7F`. It is not accepted by this connector's `issue_id` parameter

status.description: The triage state. Note the last three: an issue can be mid-deletion, mid-merge or reprocessing, which is neither open nor closed

substatus.description: Why it is in that state: `new`, `ongoing`, `regressed`, `escalating`, `archived_until_escalating`, `archived_until_condition_met`, `archived_forever`, or null. `regressed` is the one that matters in a triage flow — it means a resolved issue came back

title.description: The grouped error's title, e.g. `TypeError: undefined is not a function`

userCount.description: How many distinct users hit it — an integer, unlike `count` beside it

operations.description: Change an issue's triage state: resolve it, ignore it, or return it to unresolved. This is the state the whole organization triages against — a resolved issue leaves the unresolved queue, and an ignored one stops alerting until it recurs on Sentry's terms. Recorded in the issue's activity feed under the token's owner

params.description: The organization's slug as it appears in a Sentry URL (`acme-inc`), or its numeric id
params.name: organization_id_or_slug

params.description: `resolved` closes the issue, `ignored` mutes it until Sentry's own recurrence conditions fire, `unresolved` reopens it and puts it back in the team's queue
params.name: status

count.description: Event count, a STRING here as on the read

status.description: The state **after** this call — read it to confirm the transition applied

statusDetails.description: How the status was reached — which release resolved it, or the conditions an archive is waiting on. Free-form in the vendor's schema

substatus.description: `new`, `ongoing`, `regressed`, `escalating`, `archived_until_escalating`, `archived_until_condition_met`, `archived_forever`, or null. An `ignored` issue lands in one of the `archived_*` values, which is how the mute's terms are visible

operations.description: Get one project — its name, slug, platform, teams, DSN-bearing client keys' status and whether it is currently accepting events. This is the project an issue belongs to, so it is how a triage flow finds out which service is broken

params.description: The organization's slug as it appears in a Sentry URL (`acme-inc`), or its numeric id
params.name: organization_id_or_slug

params.description: The project's slug as it appears in a Sentry URL (`backend-api`), or its numeric id
params.name: project_id_or_slug

access.description: The permission scopes the token holds on this project

features.description: Enabled feature flags, as opaque strings

firstEvent.description: When this project first received an event, or null if it never has — which is the signal that an SDK was never wired up

id.description: The project's numeric id, as a string

isMember.description: Whether the token's own user is a member of the project

latestRelease.description: `{version}` of the most recent release seen, or null. Useful for deciding whether an error predates a deploy

name.description: The display name, which is not the slug

options.description: Per-project settings, keyed by option name. Free-form in the vendor's schema

organization.description: The owning organization, itself a large object; its `slug` is what every other operation here takes

platform.description: The SDK platform, e.g. `python`, `javascript-react`, or null

platforms.description: Every platform that has actually sent events to this project

processingIssues.description: How many processing problems the project has, e.g. missing debug symbols

slug.description: The URL slug, e.g. `backend-api` — what an issue's `project.slug` names and what this operation takes

status.description: The project's own lifecycle state — `active`, `disabled`, `pending_deletion`, `deletion_in_progress`. A non-active project explains an issue that stopped updating

team.description: `{id, name, slug}` — the owning team, or null. Deprecated in favour of `teams`

teams.description: All owning teams, each `{id, name, slug}`. This is who to notify

operations.description: Get the most recent event of an issue — the actual occurrence, with its stack trace, breadcrumbs, request context and tags. This is what makes an issue diagnosable rather than merely countable; the event list itself is excluded because it pages with an opaque cursor

params.description: The organization's slug as it appears in a Sentry URL (`acme-inc`), or its numeric id
params.name: organization_id_or_slug

contexts.description: Runtime context keyed by name (`browser`, `os`, `device`, `trace`). Free-form in the vendor's schema

dateReceived.description: When Sentry ingested it. Late-arriving events make these differ

entries.description: THE INTERESTING PART, and undocumented: the stack trace, breadcrumbs, HTTP request and message are all entries here, each shown in Sentry's examples as `{type, data}` with `type` naming which (`exception`, `stacktrace`, `breadcrumbs`, `request`, `message`). The vendor's schema declares the item as an empty schema, so nothing is asserted about `data`

errors.description: Ingest-time problems with the event itself — a missing source map, an unparseable frame — each `{type, message, data}`. Not the error the event is about

eventID.description: The same event id again, under Sentry's other spelling

groupID.description: The issue this event belongs to — the `issue_id` that fetched it. Nullable in the vendor's schema

message.description: The log message, or null for an exception-only event

nextEventID.description: The next event in the same issue, or null when this is the latest — which it is for this operation

platform.description: The SDK platform that sent it

previousEventID.description: The preceding event in the same issue, or null

release.description: The release the event came from, or null

sdk.description: `{name, version}` of the SDK that reported it, or null

size.description: The stored event's size in bytes, or null

tags.description: The event's tags as `{key, value}` pairs — **an array, not a map**. `environment`, `release`, `server_name`, `url` and `level` all arrive here, so finding the environment means searching the array for `key == "environment"`

title.description: The event's title, usually the same as the issue's

user.description: Who hit it: `{id, email, username, ip_address, name, geo, data}`, or null. **Personal data** — an IP address and an email — so read it only when the task needs it
